resolution.why: RFC 5545 §3.3.5 names the first of the two instants of a wall time a change back repeats, and §3.8.5.3 gives every occurrence the exact length DTEND less DTSTART. libical 4.0.7 places the start at the first instant (libical 4.0.6: 'Resolve local times in a fall-back overlap to the first occurrence') but gives that occurrence no length (its end equals its start). ical.js places the repeated wall time at the second instant (ical.js issue 1051) and keeps the length. So the starts follow libical and the lengths ical.js.

cases.why: 01:30 happens twice on 2019-11-03 in New York (02:00 EDT becomes 01:00 EST): the occurrence is the first, 01:30 EDT.

resolution.why: RFC 5545 §3.3.5 names the first of the two instants of a wall time a change back repeats. libical 4.0.7 places 01:45 on 2019-04-07 at the first instant, +11:00 (libical 4.0.6: 'Resolve local times in a fall-back overlap to the first occurrence'); its end, 15:45Z (02:15 at +10:30), is past the 30-minute fold, so its length is right. ical.js places it at the second instant, +10:30 (ical.js issue 1051).

cases.why: A 30-minute fold: Lord Howe goes back from 02:00 (+11:00) to 01:30 (+10:30) on 2019-04-07, so 01:45 happens twice; the occurrence is the first.

SUMMARY:dst-repeat/havana-daily-0030
DTSTART;TZID=America/Havana:20191101T003000
DTEND;TZID=America/Havana:20191101T013000
RRULE:FREQ=DAILY
END:VEVENT
END:VCALENDAR

resolution.why: RFC 5545 §3.3.5 names the first of the two instants of a wall time a change back repeats, and §3.8.5.3 gives every occurrence the exact length DTEND less DTSTART. libical 4.0.7 places the start at the first instant (libical 4.0.6: 'Resolve local times in a fall-back overlap to the first occurrence') but gives that occurrence no length (its end equals its start). ical.js places the repeated wall time at the second instant (ical.js issue 1051) and keeps the length. So the starts follow libical and the lengths ical.js.

cases.why: Midnight fold: Havana goes back from 01:00 CDT to 00:00 CST on 2019-11-03, so 00:30 happens twice; the occurrence is the first, 00:30 CDT.
